data.one_liner: Dart library for connecting to ODBC data sources and executing SQL queries.
data.what_it_does: Provides async‑first APIs to connect, run queries, fetch tables and stream large result sets via ODBC. It wraps native ODBC bindings using ffi and supports both isolate‑based non‑blocking and optional blocking clients.
use_when: You need to access an existing ODBC data source (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.) from Dart/Flutter
You require streaming of large query results without loading everything into memory
You want a single cross‑platform client that works on Windows, macOS and Linux
avoid_when: You target mobile platforms only and prefer pure Dart SQLite solutions
You need a high‑level ORM or code‑generated data models
You cannot add native ffi dependencies or need pure Dart without native libraries
strengths: Direct access to native ODBC functions for advanced use cases
weaknesses: Requires native ODBC driver manager installed on the target system
Limited to platforms where ffi is available (no web)
No built‑in ORM or code‑generation features
data.setup_notes: Install ODBC driver manager (e.g., unixODBC on Linux/macOS, native driver manager on Windows). Ensure the appropriate database driver is available and accessible. No build_runner needed, just add the package and import it.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pure Dart SQLite client for mobile and desktop, no native ODBC dependencies

alternatives.name: sqlite3
alternatives.why_pick_it: Direct SQLite bindings via ffi, suitable when SQLite is sufficient

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a higher‑level ORM‑like API on top of sqlite3 with code generation
